feedback.answered: Initial A1/A2 relationship: leaders append term/index-qualified entries, aggregate match indexes over remotes and witnesses, and request log commitment with the current term. Followers qualify replication by predecessor term, bound advertised commitment by the received suffix, and return replication support. Candidate authority is acquired through distinct votes after log freshness and vote guards; higher terms normally reset authority, lower-term messages are ignored, and reset clears votes, pending read confirmations and remote progress while preserving log history. Campaigns are blocked while committed work remains unapplied because membership may be pending. Membership application changes the quorum universe and removal can step down the leader or recalculate commitment. Snapshot handling distinguishes already committed, matching-log and actual restore cases; remotes are reconstructed separately. Engine updates send only Replicate/Ping before SaveRaftState; ordinary responses follow persistence. Ready-to-read consumption remains conditional on the matching local batch and applied index. A sourced discrepancy remains: readIndex.confirm releases a prefix of stored contexts, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation sends each remote destination the triggering message context instead of that released item's stored context, whereas local completion uses the stored context. No overlapping legal history or endpoint has been executed. An initially suspicious absence of an observer check in heartbeat response consumption is insufficient: broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends nonzero contexts only to voters. Peer.Handle also rejects responses from unknown members, and candidate vote handling rejects observers.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns indexes/term, replicates entries, consumes term-qualified member responses, and commits a quorum index only if its log term is current. Followers require predecessor agreement and never replace committed history. Engine persistence precedes ordinary replies; committed entries feed RSM application and client completion. Read authority is separately confirmed through contextual voter heartbeats, releasing stored pending requests.

context.explanation: Ticks initiate elections for eligible regular members; log freshness and one-vote rules qualify support. Candidate votes are deduplicated; peer admission excludes unknown response senders and candidate handling excludes observers. Term transitions and role resets discard pending read support, votes and remote progress. Higher-term vote suppression under a recent known leader is conditional on CheckQuorum. Transfer catches up an eligible target and invokes the ordinary election path; loss of quorum or removal can demote. Restart restores history but not leadership.

connection.explanation: New leaders retain prior log decisions but reset replication accounting, scan pending configuration work and append a current-term noop. Current-term commitment gates multi-node read confirmation. Committed-but-unapplied work blocks campaigning because it can change the quorum; RSM membership application updates raft under raftMu. Snapshot recovery restores state before remotes are reconstituted. Old-term replies are rejected; authority reset clears pending read contexts; client batches independently await correlated ready state and applied index or timeout.

after.execution_owner: raft state machine through Peer.Handle and tick
after.protocol_context: Per-cluster term, vote and role
after.trigger: Election timeout, RequestVote/response, leader messages or CheckQuorum
implementation_guards: Peer rejects unknown response senders; candidate ignores observer votes and deduplicates votes.
Vote grant requires prior-vote eligibility and last-log freshness; campaign waits for committed work to be applied.
Higher-term vote requests may be suppressed within the known-leader lease when CheckQuorum is enabled.
writes: New term clears vote; reset clears votes, pending readIndex, transfer and replication progress; durable log and commitment remain.
important_branches: Higher-term accepted messages demote; lower-term messages are ignored (leader messages can receive NoOP to unstick a candidate).
Current-term candidate receiving leader traffic becomes follower; quorum inactivity can demote the leader.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Only current leader forms commitments and confirms read contexts; reset discards pending confirmation support.

after.execution_owner: RSM membership then node/raft under raftMu
after.protocol_context: Committed configuration entry and prior membership
after.trigger: RSM configChange application
implementation_guards: Membership rejects prohibited role changes, readding removed members, stale ordered changes, invalid promotions and deletion of the only node.
writes: Accepted changes update membership, Peer voter maps and registry; pending configuration flag cleared.
important_branches: Self-removal demotes leader and requests node removal; observer promotion can inherit progress; removal may recalculate commitment.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Changes eligible quorum population and may advance commitment after removal.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Campaign waits for committed configuration application; self-removal ends leadership.

unknowns: Detailed admission and ordering options for all reconfiguration histories remain open.

after.execution_owner: engine step worker, Peer and log reader
after.protocol_context: Per-node update persistence batch
after.trigger: stepNode/GetUpdate then SaveRaftState and Commit
durable_effects: SaveRaftState receives entries, snapshot and term/vote/commit state before ordinary response sends.
important_branches: Replicate/Ping may be sent before persistence; other messages are sent afterwards.
FastApply distinguishes application work requiring newly saved entries/snapshots.
async_boundaries: Apply worker and step worker communicate through queues; Commit clears exported work and advances processed/applied bookkeeping.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Persists support before replication acknowledgements are sent.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Term and vote state are carried in the same update protocol.

unknowns: Specific backend crash atomicity and on-disk state-machine durability remain unexamined.

after.protocol_context: Local request batches keyed by SystemCtx
after.trigger: ReadIndex API queue, node step, ready response or applied/timeout update
writes: Each nonempty drained batch gets a new nonzero Low context; earlier batches remain until completion/drop/timeout.
addReady updates only the exact context batch; applied notifies success only after its positive index has applied and before deadline.
important_branches: ReadLocalNode requires successful ReadIndex readiness.
gc times out pending requests; it does not send a new ReadIndex.
async_boundaries: API return precedes outcome notification; separate step iterations permit overlapping contexts.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Produces independent contextual read requests; completion depends on the A1 authority confirmation being routed to the same batch.

unknowns: Full transport batching and forwarding adaptation paths require inspection before a harness bypasses them.

after.protocol_context: Current leader term with committed entry of that term for multi-voter reads
after.trigger: ReadIndex stores request; contextual HeartbeatResp confirms queue prefix
implementation_guards: ReadIndex requests from witnesses are dropped; multi-voter leader requires a committed current-term entry.
Nonzero heartbeat contexts are sent to voters only; confirmation deduplicates sender IDs and counts the leader implicitly.
writes: Pending records retain ctx, from and committed index; confirm removes the released prefix and raises its indexes to the confirmed record index.
external_effects: Returns local ReadyToRead or sends ReadIndexResp to each stored requester.
important_branches: Single-node quorum immediately returns ready state; multi-node path waits for confirmation.
Local released items use s.ctx, while remote messages use m.Hint/m.HintHigh for every released item.
async_boundaries: Heartbeat retries use newest pending context; message delivery can overlap multiple pending requests.
unknowns: Can remote prefix release lose per-request context in a complete legal overlapping history?

after.protocol_context: Term-qualified reply from leader
after.trigger: ReadIndexResp
writes: Marks leader available and appends ReadyToRead using received context and index.

cross_activity_effects.A7: Client pending batch selection uses the exported context, not merely destination or index.

after.execution_owner: node replay, newRaft and RSM Recover
after.protocol_context: Startup or installed snapshot
after.trigger: replayLog/Launch or snapshot recovery completion
writes: Startup reconstructs state and log range, loads membership, then enters follower/observer/witness role with fresh transient progress.
Snapshot restore rejects old indexes, can advance matching-log commitment, or replaces in-memory history; RSM recovery subsequently restores membership/remotes under raftMu.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Restores committed history and eligible participant maps without retaining old pending read support.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Startup does not resume leader authority; recovered membership controls election participation.

unknowns: Snapshot transport failures, asynchronous cancellation and disk-specific recovery variants remain open.

after.protocol_context: Per-cluster term, log and voting membership
after.trigger: Propose and Replicate/ReplicateResp
implementation_guards: Leader rejects proposals during transfer; serializes configuration proposals with pendingConfigChange.
Follower matches predecessor term and refuses changes at committed indexes.
Leader counts remotes and witnesses, excluding observers; tryCommit requires current-term entry at the quorum index.
writes: Leader assigns term/index; responses advance remote match; log commitment only advances.
external_effects: Replicate messages propagate entries and commitment; rejection feedback adjusts next and retries.
async_boundaries: Peer update messages and entries pass through the engine persistence boundary.

after.protocol_context: Existing term and target voting member
after.trigger: LeaderTransfer, catch-up response, TimeoutNow or transfer timeout
implementation_guards: Target must be a remote, not self; one transfer at a time.
writes: Transfer target set; proposals dropped until transfer abort or authority reset.
external_effects: Caught-up target receives TimeoutNow and enters normal election path through tick.

after.meaning: The local raft state is leader for its current term following election; this is local role authority, not a timeless assertion of live quorum.
after.validity_context: Until demotion, higher-term/reset transition or self-removal; CheckQuorum checks activity periodically when enabled.
after.durability: Term/vote persist through updates; leader role does not survive restart.
after.recovery: newRaft enters follower/observer/witness with no leader.

after.meaning: Local log.committed marks the prefix eligible for application; leader advancement counts a quorum at a current-term entry, while followers adopt bounded advertised commitment and snapshots can establish a committed prefix.
after.validity_context: Local log history including current snapshot; committed prefix cannot be overwritten by normal append.
after.durability: State Commit is exported for SaveRaftState; local advance can precede persistence.
after.recovery: State and snapshot reconstruct committed prefix.

after.meaning: A pending readStatus with stored requester/context is released as part of a prefix after confirmation reaches the current quorum; its returned index is the confirming record index. This does not assert correct remote encoding or client completion.
after.validity_context: Leader pending queue in one authority epoch; transient records are reset on authority transition.
after.recovery: Restart does not recover pending read confirmation records.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns indexes/term, replicates entries, consumes term-qualified member responses, and commits a quorum index only if its log term is current. Followers require predecessor agreement and never replace committed history. Engine persistence precedes ordinary replies; committed entries feed RSM application and client completion. Read authority is separately confirmed through contextual voter heartbeats, releasing stored pending requests.

context.explanation: Ticks initiate elections for eligible regular members; log freshness and one-vote rules qualify support. Candidate votes are deduplicated; peer admission excludes unknown response senders and candidate handling excludes observers. Term transitions and role resets discard pending read support, votes and remote progress. Higher-term vote suppression under a recent known leader is conditional on CheckQuorum. Transfer catches up an eligible target and invokes the ordinary election path; loss of quorum or removal can demote. Restart restores history but not leadership.

connection.explanation: New leaders retain prior log decisions but reset replication accounting, scan pending configuration work and append a current-term noop. Current-term commitment gates multi-node read confirmation. Committed-but-unapplied work blocks campaigning because it can change the quorum; RSM membership application updates raft under raftMu. Snapshot recovery restores state before remotes are reconstituted. Old-term replies are rejected; authority reset clears pending read contexts; client batches independently await correlated ready state and applied index or timeout.

open_details: Remote read-prefix responses use triggering context rather than each released context; legal overlap and responsibility need a fixed investigation.
Storage backend crash behavior, snapshot transfer failure variants, session completion and concurrent reconfiguration details remain open.
after.rationale: Representative formation and authority paths include their persistence, membership, recovery and application boundaries; local anomalies and deeper variants remain open.

after.system_boundary: Captured Dragonboat Go module: NodeHost/node engine, internal raft, RSM, persistence and transport integration; application implementations remain caller-supplied but their in-repository adapters remain in scope.

selections.rationale: Fix the sourced per-operation correlation responsibility before executing a history. The oracle will use independent requester identity and original SystemCtx; it will not infer a global liveness obligation.

feedback.answered: Ordinary read request/response dispatch does not serialize completion across contexts. The captured identity interface and exact-context consumer establish an operation-correlation duty when pending records are released. Persistence ordering for the future driver is explicit in Update: store state/entries before sending non-replication messages.
remaining: A controlled Peer history must observe actual admission, quorum release, emitted replies and destination ReadyToRead without injecting private pending records or fabricated acknowledgements.
feedback.rationale: The obligation concerns correspondence at a completed protocol action; it neither assumes all reads succeed nor claims finite waiting proves stalling.

B-read-client.rationale: Resolve the previously unread ordinary-message dispatch premise and make the operation identity interface explicit.
B-read-client.preserves: The principal Fact, its producer/consumer edges and the candidate's remote response-correlation question are unchanged; dispatch adds no completion barrier and does not change admissible overlap.
